decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit extends the firm's core airfield lighting business, was promoted as setting new industry standards and has long airport replacement cycles, so it likely meets aspirations and gives no trigger for problemistic search.

The air situation display complements the tower and surveillance portfolio and fits the integrated-operations strategy, so with the industry growing and the firm hiring there is enough slack to carry it.
The airport systems training program is a low-cost service tied to the installed base that supports customer lock-in, so dropping it would release few resources.

The airfield ground lighting course supports the firm's core lighting business, and although it is less visible and might be folded into the broader training offer, its low cost makes continuation likely.

The collaboration software is central to the stated move toward collaborative decision-making and integrated operations, so management would keep it despite uncertain early results, since slack allows it.
As the flagship multilateration system aligned with the firm's direction, it would be judged against long-term strategic aspirations rather than short-term shortfalls and kept.
